title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
gist: Cilium 1.20 broadens Kubernetes Gateway API support (1.4 to 1.6, adding ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS, TCPRoute, UDPRoute), opens its eBPF datapath to beta third-party plugins developed by Google, adds auto selection of netkit versus veth, and advances ztunnel-based sidecarless mTLS with SPIRE support.

insights.claim: Cilium 1.20 moves from Gateway API 1.4 to 1.6, adding ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS filtering, TCPRoute and UDPRoute, bringing HTTP authentication and non-HTTP services such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Cilium is widening from CNI into a full traffic-management layer, competing with ingress and mesh vendors.
insights.quote: Gateway API becomes a much broader traffic management layer.
insights.locator: Cilium moves from Gateway API 1.4 to 1.6

insights.claim: ExternalAuth lets an HTTPRoute consult an external authorisation service that can forward, redirect to login, or reject a request and pass identity headers, while TCPRoute and UDPRoute remove the need to fall back to LoadBalancer or NodePort Services for Layer 4 traffic.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Moves auth and L4 routing into declarative Kubernetes config, reducing bespoke ingress setups.
insights.locator: According to Vibert and Chaiehloudj, ExternalAuth

insights.claim: ListenerSets let application teams add listeners from their own namespaces while the platform team keeps control of the shared Gateway, which one platform engineer said removes a platform bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Reduces central-team change tickets for new hostnames or ports, easing platform scaling.
insights.locator: ListenerSets address a separate ownership problem

insights.claim: Kubernetes community recommends Gateway API as organisations move away from the retired Ingress NGINX controller, and AWS reached general availability of Gateway API support in its Load Balancer Controller, while Cilium differs by offering CNI, service networking and gateway in one project.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Ingress NGINX retirement is pushing migration to Gateway API, a tailwind for implementations.
insights.locator: The direction is consistent with work elsewhere in Kubernetes networking

insights.claim: Cilium's eBPF datapath now accepts third-party plugins running as separate processes, built and upgraded independently and connected via a small custom resource and gRPC, where previously cloud providers had to upstream changes or maintain forks.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Lowers fork maintenance for cloud providers and may deepen Cilium's role as a networking platform.
insights.quote: Datapath plugins, developed by Google, make Cilium less like a sealed networking appliance and more like a network operating system.
insights.locator: A second change opens Cilium's eBPF datapath

insights.claim: The datapath plugin mechanism is beta, intended for operators with detailed Cilium internals knowledge, and can break Cilium or weaken security with maintainers possibly needing to update code as internals change.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Not a general extension system; production risk remains for early adopters.

insights.claim: Setting bpf.datapathMode=auto makes each Cilium agent test its host at start-up, use netkit where supported (Linux 6.8 or later) and fall back to veth, avoiding separate node pools for mixed kernel fleets; the default remains veth.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Eases rollout of netkit for performance without fleet segmentation.
insights.locator: Cilium 1.20 also introduces automatic selection of the pod datapath

insights.claim: Cilium's ztunnel in 1.20 adds a choice between an internal certificate authority and SPIRE-issued workload identities, plus Prometheus metrics, and holds new connections while establishing TLS 1.3 over an HBONE tunnel to avoid first-packet loss seen in the older mutual-authentication design.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Sidecarless mTLS is maturing in Cilium, competing directly with Istio ambient mode.
insights.locator: The fourth main area is ztunnel

insights.claim: Cilium's ztunnel builds on the ztunnel project originally created for Istio's ambient mode, remains beta, and the older Mutual Authentication feature is now deprecated, with release notes flagging action for Kafka-aware policies, Envoy Go extensions and custom CNI configuration users.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Upgrade planning needed for users of deprecated features; convergence on Istio's ztunnel.
insights.locator: This has parallels with Istio's ambient mode
